Summarise an edge weight model

Source: R/bison_model.R
summary.bison_model.Rd

Summarises a fitted edge model: the posterior median and credible interval of each edge weight, and of any other effects in the model. A credible interval contains the true value with the given probability, according to the model. Use summary() to check the estimates after fitting with bison_model().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'bison_model'
summary(object, ci = 0.9, transform = TRUE, ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted bison_model object.

ci

Width of the credible interval, e.g. 0.9 for a 90% interval.

transform

If TRUE (the default), edge weights are reported on the natural scale (probabilities for binary models, rates for count models). If FALSE, they're on the link scale used inside the model (log-odds for binary models, log rates for count models). In models with an intercept or other effects, the natural-scale values are for an observation where those effects are 0.

...

Not used.

Value

A summary.bison_model object. Printing it shows, for each dyad, the posterior median edge weight and the lower and upper bounds of the credible interval, followed by any other effects in the model (see get_effects()).

See also

get_edgelist() to get the edge weights as a data frame.

Examples

sim_data <- simulate_bison_model("binary", aggregated = TRUE)
fit_edge <- bison_model(
  (event | effort) ~ dyad(node_1_id, node_2_id),
  data = sim_data$df_sim,
  model_type = "binary_conjugate",
  priors = get_default_priors("binary_conjugate")
)
summary(fit_edge, ci = 0.95)
